title: BDCs: Not All Yield Is Created Equal
author: Michael Lebowitz
description: Business Development Corporations (BDCs) offer attractive yields but require careful analysis. Unlike private credit funds, BDCs trade on stock exchanges providing liquidity, though with daily price volatility. Key evaluation factors include Net Asset Value discounts/premiums, internal vs. external management, portfolio composition (especially software exposure), capital structure, PIK income ratios, and dividend coverage. Current market sentiment has pushed many quality BDCs to discounts, creating potential opportunities for informed investors.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Blackstone Credit & Insurance BDC trades at a discount to NAV, has slightly better credit quality with extremely low non-accrual rates, uses first lien senior secured loans with structural protection, and benefits from Blackstone's scale and expertise. The discount presents a potential opportunity despite external management structure.

Main Street Capital has internal management (avoiding principal-agent problems), a proven track record of consistent NAV growth, conservative leverage (47% debt/53% equity), and extremely low non-accrual rates. Trades at significant premium to NAV reflecting investor confidence, though lower yield due to valuation.

title: Skip Buying a Rental Property. Investing $90,000 in These Stocks Could Make You Over $7,000 in Annual Passive Income.
author: Keith Speights
description: The article suggests skipping rental properties and instead investing $90,000 in three high-yield dividend stocks - Realty Income, Ares Capital, and Blackstone Secured Lending Fund - which could generate over $7,000 in annual passive income.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Realty Income is a REIT that owns over 15,600 properties and pays a monthly dividend with a forward yield of 5.67%. It has increased its dividend for 30 consecutive years, indicating a stable and growing income stream.

Ares Capital is the largest publicly traded business development company (BDC) and pays a forward dividend yield of 8.6%. It has a diversified investment portfolio and a lower-than-average annual loss rate, suggesting reliable and consistent income.

Blackstone Secured Lending Fund is a BDC with the financial backing of Blackstone, the world's largest alternative asset manager. It offers a forward dividend yield of 9.25% and has high earnings quality, credit quality, and low expenses, making it an attractive income-generating investment.
